newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak bank PKB raises basic cap to SKK 1.0 bln.
newsitem.headline: Slovak bank PKB raises basic cap to SKK 1.0 bln.

text.p: Prva Komunalna Banka (PKB) a.s., Slovakia's ninth largest bank, on Wednesday said it had increased its basic capital by 500 million crowns to 1.002 billion.

"On January 31, our bank succesfully completed an increase of its basic capital, which now totals 1.002 billion crowns," PKB spokeswoman Jaroslava Kremenova told Reuters. She declined to provide any further details on the equity increase.

According to the official news agency TASR, the move was to have been made through an issue of non-publicly traded shares and that it should be the first step toward the bank's aim of being granted a licence for providing mortgage loans.
PKB carries a BB+ senior debt rating by Thomson BankWatch, assigned last month.
Thomson has also assigned PKB with an LC-2 short-term local currency debt rating to PKB, saying the bank has been showing favourable financial trends and success as a "niche player".
PKB is a three-year old private universal bank, specialising mainly in providing complex services to the municipal sector
On Tuesday, the bank said it would launch a one billion crown tranche of four-year bonds on February 17. The bonds will pay an annual fixed coupon of 12.5 percent.
